summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of John Shuter, a cricketer born in 1855 in Thornton Heath, Surrey, who died in 1920 in Blackheath, Kent. He played cricket for England and Surrey in the late 19th century. The note highlights his captaincy of Surrey during a run of County Championship successes and describes him as an off-side batsman.
one_line: John Shuter was a late 19th-century English cricketer who captained Surrey to several County Championship titles.
key_facts: John Shuter was born on 9 February 1855 in Thornton Heath, Surrey, England.
John Shuter died on 5 July 1920 in Blackheath, Kent, England.
Shuter was a cricketer who played for England and Surrey in the late 19th century.
Shuter is best remembered for captaining Surrey to a string of County Championship wins around the time the championship became official in 1890.
Bowler George Lohmann aided Surrey's championship success under Shuter's captaincy.
John Sharpe and William Lockwood also supported Surrey's championship wins under Shuter.
Shuter first led Surrey to the County Championship in 1887.
Surrey came first in the County Championship in 1888.
Surrey tied with Lancashire and Nottinghamshire in the County Championship in 1889.
Surrey won the County Championship again in 1890, 1891 and 1892.
Shuter was a batsman and chiefly an off-side player.
